The source text is a nine-line teaching on the metaphysics of speech as a manifestation of divine gevurot, the danger of harsh gevurot falling on the tzaddik of the generation, and the tzaddik's two methods for sweetening them (judging favorably or accepting suffering with love). The historical centerpiece is the explanation of why the Baal Shem Tov passed away — harsh speech from Sabbatean scholars fell on him as the gadol ha-dor. The teaching contains two additional bechina clusters beyond the dataset edge: (1) the identity of Torah she-be'al peh with the tzaddik ha-dor and the talmid chakham, explicitly declared as 'one thing' in line 8; (2) the identity of the sweetened-speech Torah with torat chesed, grounded in the Talmudic definition (Sukkah 49b). The primary dataset edge (דיבורים = גבורות) anchors Package 1. The two source-text bechinas (Torah = tzaddik, Torah = torat chesed) form Package 2.

packages.label: דִּבּוּרִים וּגְבוּרוֹת — הַדִּבּוּר כְּבָחִינַת גְּבוּרָה
packages.label_en: Speech and Gevurot — Speech as an Aspect of Divine Severity
packages.reason: The foundational bechina of Torah #207 is the opening statement: 'כָּל הַדִּבּוּרִים הֵם בְּחִינַת גְּבוּרוֹת' — all speech is an aspect of gevurot. The proof is twofold: the verse 'וּגְבוּרָתְךָ יְדַבֵּרוּ' (Psalm 145:11) links speaking and gevurot linguistically; and the kabbalistic writings (the Ari) teach that the five gevurot of da'at break through the mouth and become the five articulatory organs of speech (five motzaot ha-peh). Neither produces the other — they are two faces of the same spiritual reality: speech is the external, audible form of the gevurot that exist within da'at. This is a textbook bechina: symmetric, reversible, identity of essential nature across two domains (the physical domain of speech / the Kabbalistic domain of the sefirot's gevurot). The polarity is neutral rather than good or evil because speech itself is an object or instrument — it can serve either holiness (Torah study and good words that sweeten the gevurot) or evil (harsh speech that falls on the tzaddik). The teaching makes this ambivalence explicit: the same reality (speech = gevurot) can be sweetened through Torah and good words, or remain unsweetened and cause damage. The five motzaot ha-peh (five organs of speech: aleph/glottal, bet/labial, gimel/palatal, dalet/dental, vav/lingual) are implicitly included in this package as the structural bridge between the internal gevurot and the external speech — they are not given an independent bechina node but are referenced as the mechanism by which gevurot emerge as speech.

The teaching returns to this bechina equation five times across the nine lines (lines 1, 2, 3, 4, 5), each time restating it in a new context (normal speech, harsh gevurot, the tzaddik's burden). This repeated restatement confirms the centrality of this package — it is the Torah's foundational axiom.

The term 'גבורות קשות' (harsh gevurot) in lines 2–7 is a specification of גבורות (the same node, at the extreme end of severity) rather than a separate node. The Rebbe says 'sometimes harsh gevurot emerge' — indicating that 'גבורות קשות' is a mode or intensity of the same category of גבורות, not a distinct concept with different essential nature.

The five motzaot ha-peh (מוצאות הפה) and the five gevurot of da'at are cited as the mechanistic explanation for the bechina, not as independent bechina nodes themselves. They appear in line 1 as proof ('כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּכְּתָבִים') and are absorbed into the foundational equation.

No evil mirror is developed for this package. The 'evil' dimension of this Torah is expressed through the eitza flow (harsh gevurot → unsweetened speech → falls on tzaddik), not through a separate bechina cluster. The polarity of speech/gevurot is appropriately neutral.

packages.label: תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, הַצַּדִּיק, וְתוֹרַת חֶסֶד
packages.label_en: Oral Torah, the Tzaddik, and the Torah of Lovingkindness
packages.reason: Line 8 contains the Torah's second structural bechina cluster, built on two explicit identity declarations: (1) speaking against Torah she-be'al peh and speaking against the tzaddik ha-dor 'is literally one thing' (הוּא דָּבָר אֶחָד מַמָּשׁ) — because the essence of Oral Torah depends entirely on the tzaddik ha-dor, and (2) 'הַתַּלְמִיד חָכָם הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ הַתּוֹרָה' — the Torah scholar IS himself the Torah (from the Talmudic statement in Makkot 22b: 'How foolish are those who stand before the Torah scroll but not before a Torah scholar'). These are bechina equations of essential nature: Torah she-be'al peh and the tzaddik ha-dor are not in a cause-effect relationship — they are two expressions of the same spiritual reality. Neither produces the other; both are manifestations of the living, embodied divine teaching-presence. Line 9 extends this cluster: when the tzaddik sweetens the harsh speech, he 'transforms the words into Torah' — and this Torah is specifically תּוֹרַת חֶסֶד (Torah of lovingkindness). The definition cited from Sukkah 49b ('זֶה הַלּוֹמֵד עַל מְנָת לְלַמְּדָהּ' — one who studies in order to teach others) is a bechina identity statement: torat chesed IS Torah that is taught to others, and this IS what the sweetened speech becomes. Thus three nodes share the same essential nature: תורה שבעל פה (the living Oral Torah), צדיק הדור (the tzaddik who embodies it), and תורת חסד (the Torah of kindness produced when he sweetens harsh gevurot and teaches them). The dominant node is תורה שבעל פה because it appears at the center of both bechina statements in line 8, and because the entire teaching builds toward explaining why speaking against it is so devastating. The polarity is unambiguously good: this package defines the holy domain — Torah, its human embodiment, and its most sublime form (torat chesed).

תורה שבעל פה and צדיק הדור: Line 8 states explicitly: 'כְּשֶׁמְּדַבְּרִים עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה, אוֹ כְּשֶׁמְּדַבְּרִים עַל הַצַּדִּיק הַדּוֹר בְּעַצְמוֹ, הוּא דָּבָר אֶחָד מַמָּשׁ' — speaking against Oral Torah or against the tzaddik of the generation is one and the same thing. The reasoning given: 'עִקַּר תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה הוּא תָּלוּי בְּצַדִּיק הַדּוֹר' (the essence of Oral Torah depends on/is rooted in the tzaddik of the generation). This is a bechina of shared essence: Oral Torah and the tzaddik are not cause-and-effect — they are co-expressions of the same living divine teaching-presence. The Zohar proof cited ('שְׁכִינְתָּא בֵּין תְּרֵין צַדִּיקַיָּא יָתֵבָא') is given as the mystical basis for this identity.

תורה שבעל פה and תלמיד חכם: Line 8 continues: 'הַתַּלְמִיד חָכָם הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ הַתּוֹרָה' — the Torah scholar is himself the Torah. The Talmud (Makkot 22b) proves this: one should stand before a Torah scholar just as one stands before a Torah scroll, because the scholar IS the Torah. This is the same identity as between תורה שבעל פה and צדיק הדור, expressed from the angle of the individual scholar rather than the generation's leader.

תורה שבעל פה and תורת חסד: Line 9 states that when the tzaddik sweetens the harsh words, he 'makes Torah from the words' — and this is specifically תּוֹרַת חֶסֶד, defined via Sukkah 49b as 'the one who studies in order to teach others.' The sweetened Torah is the ultimate form of Torah she-be'al peh — the living Torah that the tzaddik transmits outward. The connection: the same Oral Torah that was attacked by harsh speech, when sweetened and transformed, becomes the Torah of lovingkindness that the tzaddik teaches. This is a within-domain bechina: the sweetened form (torat chesed) IS the positive actualization of the same reality (Torah she-be'al peh).

צדיק הדור vs. גדול הדור: The teaching uses both terms. 'גדול הדור' appears in lines 2, 4, 5, 7 and refers to the same person as 'צַדִּיק הַדּוֹר' (lines 5, 8). In line 7 the Baal Shem Tov is called 'הַגָּדוֹל הַדּוֹר'. These are treated as synonyms — the same conceptual node, the leader of the generation who carries the burden of the gevurot. No separate bechina is needed; they are textual aliases for the same node.

Evil mirror check: This Torah does not develop an explicit evil bechina counterpart for Package 2. The opposing force is the Sabbatean heretics (Sha'tz) and the scholars who left the fold — but these are described as eitza-agents (they caused harsh speech to fall on the Besht) rather than as a conceptual bechina cluster. There is no equation of the form 'the false sage IS an aspect of X.' The evil dimension of this Torah operates entirely at the eitza level, not through a bechina package.

stats.good_evil_mirror: Torah #207 does not develop an evil bechina package. The negative dimension — harsh gevurot, Sabbatean heretics, scholars who left the fold — operates entirely through the eitza chain (harsh gevurot → unsweetened speech → falls on tzaddik). The Sha'tz and his seduced scholars are presented as agents of historical causation, not as a bechina cluster with shared essential nature. The evil mirror of Package 2 (Torah = tzaddik = torat chesed) would be: false teaching = false leader = destructive speech. But the Rebbe does not develop this into explicit bechina equations — he describes it narratively as a series of cause-and-effect events. This is consistent with the Torah's practical orientation: its goal is to explain and guide the tzaddik's response to gevurot, not to map the ontology of evil.

stats.teaching_structure: Torah #207 is a nine-line practical-mystical teaching on the spiritual mechanics of speech. It has a clear three-part structure: (1) Lines 1–2: The foundational axiom (speech = gevurot) and the entry of harsh gevurot into the world through the great sages. (2) Lines 3–7: The two scenarios — sweetened (tzaddik judges favorably or accepts suffering) vs. unsweetened (harsh words fall on tzaddik, causing fall or death), illustrated by the Baal Shem Tov's passing. (3) Lines 8–9: The theological depth — why this matters (Torah she-be'al peh IS the tzaddik IS the talmid chakham) and the redemptive outcome (sweetened speech becomes torat chesed). The teaching is oriented toward the tzaddik/gadol ha-dor as its primary audience, offering both explanation and practice.
